name: Veal Pudding
description: Historical recipe from The Whitehouse Cookbook (1887). Source method; not modernized or kitchen-tested.

ingredients.name: about two pounds of lean veal
ingredients.originalText: about two pounds of lean veal

ingredients.name: piece of butter the size of an egg
ingredients.originalText: a piece of butter the size of an egg

instructions.text: Cut about two pounds of lean veal into small collops a quarter of an inch in thickness
Put a piece of butter the size of an egg into a very clean frying pan to melt
Lay in the veal and a few slices of bacon, a small sprig of thyme and a seasoning of pepper and salt
Place the pan over a slow fire for about ten minutes, then add two or three spoonfuls of warm water
Just boil it up and then let it stand to cool
Line a pudding-dish with a good suet crust
Lay in the veal and bacon, pour the gravy over it
Roll out a piece of paste to form a lid, place it over, press it close with the thumb
Tie the basin in a pudding cloth and put it into a saucepan of boiling water, keeping continually boiling until done, or about one hour

source.author: F.L. Gillette
source.originalInstructions:
1. Cut about two pounds of lean veal into small collops a quarter of an inch in thickness
2. Put a piece of butter the size of an egg into a very clean frying pan to melt
3. Lay in the veal and a few slices of bacon, a small sprig of thyme and a seasoning of pepper and salt
4. Place the pan over a slow fire for about ten minutes, then add two or three spoonfuls of warm water
5. Just boil it up and then let it stand to cool
6. Line a pudding-dish with a good suet crust
7. Lay in the veal and bacon, pour the gravy over it
8. Roll out a piece of paste to form a lid, place it over, press it close with the thumb
9. Tie the basin in a pudding cloth and put it into a saucepan of boiling water, keeping continually boiling until done, or about one hour
